case: MongoDB missing sparse-document fields remain distinct from BSON null
outcome: Explicit safe marker: absent fields map to Value::Undecodable("missing BSON field"), explicit BSON null maps to Value::Null, and the marker is refused by the MongoDB binding path.

regressions.assertions: MongoDB 7 stores one document with explicit BSON null and one without the field. Independent native reads verify presence/absence. The driver query is indexed by _id and requires Value::Null versus the distinct missing-field marker.
regressions.before_fix: Failed: absent field decoded as Value::Null. See before-fix.txt.
regressions.after_fix: Passed in focused Docker execution and the complete MongoDB crate test run.

regressions.assertions: The distinct absent-field marker is refused by value_to_bson instead of being converted to BSON null.

commands.focused: rtk cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-driver-mongodb --test integration value_contracts::value_contract_mongodb_missing_fields_remain_distinct_from_bson_null -- --include-ignored --exact --test-threads=1
commands.clippy: rtk cargo clippy --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-driver-mongodb --all-targets -- -D warnings

results.before_fix: Expected failure at the absent-field assertion: left Value::Null, right Value::Undecodable("missing BSON field").

remaining: The shared Value model has no dedicated Missing variant; this case deliberately uses the existing safe undecodable/refusal marker and does not claim exact generic missing-value support.
MongoDB browse census cost, writes to already-observed documents during the cursor, and run_find separate-read consistency remain open.
This case does not close the B3 engine/type/consumer matrix or any B4/installed release gate.
